subject: interpretation of sem results when data are binary

messages.author: cf19475e9feb9344
messages.subject: interpretation of sem results when data are binary
parts:
Hi all,

Does anyone know how to interpret the results  of a SEM when all variables are binary? I used the link="logit" when fitting the model. I presume the estimates are in log odds aren't they? Can you please tell me how to interpret the estimates for Thresholds?

Attached is the output of the model.

I'd also like to know how to assess the fitness of the model

Many thanks in advance
Vasilis

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: interpretation of sem results when data are binary
parts:
On 05/01/2014 03:56 PM, vasilis nikolaou wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Does anyone know how to interpret the results of a SEM when all
> variables are binary? I used the link="logit" when fitting the model.

The 'link' argument is just a placeholder, and will only be used when
estimator is MML (marginal ML). It is ignored for all other estimator.

By default, lavaan uses the WLSMV estimator, and here we use the
"probit" link.

You will need to find yourself a good book and/or tutorial to help you
with the interpretation of probits and thresholds.

Yves.
